# The shipped builds

*Generated by `content/builds/archetypes/generate.py`: do not edit by hand.*

Thirty archetypes in `content/builds/archetypes/`, each a whole build (engine, car, tune) that starts, idles, pulls through the gears and stops, with every part of the model switched on and standard-day air (15 C, 101.3 kPa). Their names say what they are, not whose they are; the dimensions are published figures of engines of each kind, named in each build's notes. The engines, cars and tunes are also in `content/builds/parts/` to mix: an engine in another car, a tune on another engine.

## Each build

**3.0 L straight six, twin turbo** (`straight-six-twin-turbo-30.json`). A modern 3 L twin-turbo straight six with direct injection: 84 x 89.6 mm (2979 cc), 10.2:1, four valves, both cams phased, two twin-scroll turbos each fed by three cylinders at about 1 bar. Production engines of this kind make 250 to 340 kW and 450 to 600 N m (makers' figures). In a rear-drive sports sedan with a seven-speed dual clutch.

**Flat-plane 4.5 L V8** (`flat-plane-v8-45.json`). A high-revving flat-plane V8: 94 x 81 mm (4497 cc), 12.5:1, direct injection, four valves, 9000 rpm (the published figures of the 4.5 L 90-degree flat-plane V8 of 2009, F136-type: 419 kW at 9000 rpm, 540 N m at 6000; Wikipedia and the maker's site). Variable-length runners. In a mid-engined coupe.

**Air-cooled flat six** (`air-cooled-flat-six-36.json`). A 3.6 L air- and oil-cooled flat six, two valves a cylinder on rockers, dry sump: 100 x 76.4 mm (3600 cc), 11.3:1; 184 kW at 6100 rpm and 310 N m at 4800 (the 1989 M64-type engine; Wikipedia, auto-data.net). The cooling fan's whir is the viscous fan. In a rear-engined coupe, five-speed manual.

**Big-block 7.4 L pushrod V8** (`big-block-74-pushrod-v8.json`). A 1970-era 454 cubic inch big block: 4.25 x 4.00 in (107.95 x 101.6 mm, 7440 cc), 10.25:1, two valves on pushrods and a flat-tappet hydraulic cam, one four-barrel-sized throttle over a single plenum. Rated some 250 to 300 kW net and 650 N m (makers' net figures of the era; gross ratings were 20 % higher). In a heavy muscle car with a three-speed automatic.

**Rotary twin** (`rotary-twin-13.json`). A twin-rotor Wankel, 2 x 654 cc, 9.0:1, with two sequential turbos (the 13B-REW kind: 206 to 280 PS, the latter at 6500 rpm, some 294 N m at 5000; Wikipedia, makers' figures, firm to 10 %). In a light rear-drive coupe.

**1.6 L 16-valve hot hatch** (`hot-hatch-16-16v.json`). A light front-drive hatch with a twin-cam 16-valve 1.6: 81 x 77.4 mm (1595 cc), 10.4:1; engines of the kind made 85 to 118 kW at 6500 to 7600 rpm and 140 to 160 N m (makers' figures of the 1980s and 90s).

**Supercharged 6.2 L V8** (`supercharged-v8-62.json`). The 6.2 L pushrod V8 of 103.25 x 92 mm (6162 cc) at 9.1:1 under a 1.9 L positive-displacement blower at some 0.6 bar (the LSA kind: 415 kW at 6100 rpm, 746 N m at 3800; gmauthority.com, a community spec table for the compression). In a heavy six-speed coupe.

**Small-block 5.7 L, carburettor-like** (`small-block-57-carb.json`). A 350 cubic inch small block (4.00 x 3.48 in: 101.6 x 88.4 mm, 5733 cc), 9:1, two valves on pushrods, a flat-tappet cam, one big throttle over an open plenum as a four-barrel carburettor's. Some 150 to 200 kW net and 400 to 450 N m (makers' net ratings of the 1970s and 80s). Four-speed manual, live axle.

**V10 5.2 L** (`v10-52.json`). A 90-degree V10 with split crankpins for even firing: 84.5 x 92.8 mm (5204 cc), 12.5:1, direct and port injection, 8700 rpm (the 5.2 L V10 of 2008 on: 386 to 470 kW at 8000 to 8700 rpm, 530 to 565 N m at 6500; makers' figures). In an all-wheel-drive mid-engined car.

**V12 6.5 L** (`v12-65.json`). A naturally aspirated 6.5 L V12 of the 2010s: 95 x 76.4 mm (6496 cc), 13.5:1, direct injection, four valves, all cams phased (engines of the kind: 515 to 588 kW at 8250 to 9000 rpm, 690 to 720 N m at 6000 to 7000; makers' figures). In a front-mid-engined GT with a seven-speed dual clutch.

**Inline five turbo rally** (`inline-five-turbo-rally.json`). A 2.2 L 20-valve straight five, 81 x 86.4 mm (2226 cc), 9.3:1 (the 3B kind: 162 kW at 5700 rpm, 309 N m road trim; audiworld.com), here in rally trim: 1.3 bar, anti-lag, a spark-cut limiter, race fuel; rally engines of the kind made some 220 to 260 kW. Sequential gearbox, all-wheel drive.

**Boxer four turbo with unequal headers** (`boxer-four-turbo-unequal.json`). A 2.5 L boxer four with one turbo, 99.5 x 79 mm (2457 cc), 8.2:1 (the EJ257 kind: 221 kW at 6000 rpm, 393 N m at 4000; Wikipedia and enthusiasts' tables). Its headers' primaries of unequal length are the burble: written in the exhaust builder (primSpread), which the program does not yet run. All-wheel drive, six-speed manual.

**Two-stage-cam 2.0 L** (`two-stage-cam-20.json`). A 2.0 L four with two cam profiles a valve switched at 6000 rpm: 87 x 84 mm (1997 cc), 11.7:1, 9000 rpm (the F20C kind: 176 kW at 8300 rpm, 208 N m at 7500; makers' figures, from memory, firm to 5 %; the B16A's switch point of 5500 rpm: global.honda). In a light rear-drive roadster.

**Kei 660 cc triple turbo** (`kei-660-triple-turbo.json`). A Japanese kei-class three: 68 x 60.4 mm (658 cc), 8.6:1, four valves, a small turbo (the K6A kind: 47 kW (the class's 64 PS cap) at 6500 rpm, 103 to 108 N m at 3500; Wikipedia, goo-net-exchange). In a 780 kg rear-drive sports kei.

**Diesel 2.0 L common rail** (`diesel-20-common-rail.json`). A 2.0 L four-valve common-rail diesel with a variable-vane turbo: 81 x 95.5 mm (1968 cc), 16.5:1 (engines of the kind: 103 to 125 kW at 3500 to 4000 rpm, 320 to 380 N m from 1750; makers' figures). Balance shafts. In a front-drive family car, six-speed manual.

**Highway tractor 15 L** (`tractor-15-inline-six.json`). A 15 L straight-six truck diesel: 137 x 169 mm (14.9 L), 17:1, one variable-vane turbo; its compression brake is left off until the ECU can switch it (the X15 kind: 298 to 451 kW, 1966 to 2779 N m at 900 to 1000 rpm, governed at 1900 to 2100, idle 600 to 700; cummins.com, international.com). In a 36 t tractor-trailer, eighteen speeds.

**1.0 L three-cylinder turbo** (`three-cylinder-10-turbo.json`). A downsized 1.0 L three with a small turbo and direct injection: 71.9 x 82 mm (999 cc), 10:1 (engines of the kind: 74 to 103 kW at 5500 to 6000 rpm, 170 to 205 N m from 1500; makers' figures). In a small hatch, six-speed manual.

**1.5 L economy four** (`economy-four-15.json`). A 1.5 L naturally aspirated four of a compact car: 75 x 84.7 mm (1497 cc), 11:1, an intake cam phaser (engines of the kind: 80 to 96 kW at 6000 to 6600 rpm, 140 to 155 N m at 4300; makers' figures). Through a CVT.

**2.0 L turbo four, direct injection** (`turbo-four-20-gdi.json`). A 2.0 L direct-injection turbo four: 82.5 x 92.8 mm (1984 cc), 9.6:1 (engines of the kind in hot hatches: 155 to 228 kW at 5000 to 6500 rpm, 350 to 400 N m from 1600 to 4500; makers' figures). Front drive, six-speed dual clutch.

**3.5 L V6** (`v6-35-na.json`). A 60-degree 3.5 L V6 of a family car: 94 x 83 mm (3456 cc), 10.8:1, four valves and phased cams (engines of the kind: 195 to 224 kW at 6200 to 6600 rpm, 340 to 360 N m at 4700; makers' figures). Front drive, six-speed automatic.

**3.5 L twin-turbo V6 pickup** (`v6-35-twin-turbo-pickup.json`). A 3.5 L twin-turbo V6 of a full-size pickup: 92.5 x 86.6 mm (3497 cc), 10.5:1, direct injection, a turbo a bank (engines of the kind: 280 to 300 kW at 5000 to 6000 rpm, 640 to 690 N m at 3500; makers' figures). Four-wheel drive, ten-speed automatic.

**1.8 L twin-cam roadster** (`twin-cam-roadster-18.json`). A 1.8 L twin-cam 16-valve four: 83 x 85 mm (1839 cc), 10:1 (engines of the kind in light roadsters: 96 to 110 kW at 6500 to 7000 rpm, 160 to 170 N m at 5000; makers' figures). Rear drive, six-speed manual.

**6.7 L straight-six turbo diesel pickup** (`pickup-diesel-67-inline-six.json`). A 6.7 L straight-six turbo diesel, 107 x 124 mm (6690 cc), 16.2:1, pushrods and four valves, a variable-vane turbo (engines of the kind: 260 to 310 kW at 2800 to 3000 rpm, 1000 to 1460 N m at 1600 to 1800; makers' figures). In a heavy-duty pickup, six-speed automatic.

**Twin-turbo 4.0 L hot-vee V8** (`twin-turbo-hot-vee-v8-40.json`). A 4.0 L crossplane V8 with both turbos in the vee (hot-vee): 86 x 86 mm (3996 cc), 10.5:1, direct injection (engines of the kind: 350 to 470 kW at 5500 to 6500 rpm, 700 to 850 N m from 2000 to 4500; makers' figures). All-wheel drive, eight-speed automatic.

**Narrow-angle VR6 2.8 L** (`vr6-28.json`). A 15-degree narrow-angle six, one head over both banks, two valves a cylinder: 81 x 90.3 mm (2792 cc), 10:1 (the 12-valve VR6 of 1991: 128 kW at 5800 rpm, 235 N m at 4200; makers' figures, from memory, firm to 5 %). In a front-drive hatch.

**3.2 L straight six, high-revving** (`straight-six-32-high-rev.json`). A naturally aspirated 3.2 L straight six with a throttle body a cylinder: 87 x 91 mm (3246 cc), 11.5:1, 8000 rpm (the S54 kind: 252 kW at 7900 rpm, 365 N m at 4900; makers' figures, from memory, firm to 5 %). Rear drive, six-speed manual.

**Four-cam 5.0 L V8** (`four-cam-v8-50.json`). A 5.0 L four-cam crossplane V8: 93 x 92.7 mm (5038 cc), 12:1, all four cams phased (engines of the kind: 300 to 343 kW at 6500 to 7000 rpm, 530 to 570 N m at 4250 to 4600; makers' figures). Rear drive, six-speed manual.

**7.0 L pushrod V8, dry sump** (`big-bore-70-pushrod-v8.json`). A 7.0 L small-block-sized pushrod V8 with titanium intake valves and a dry sump: 104.8 x 101.6 mm (7011 cc), 11:1, 7000 rpm (the LS7 kind: 377 kW at 6300 rpm, 637 N m at 4800; gmauthority.com). In a light front-engined sports car, six-speed manual.

**3.8 L pushrod V6** (`pushrod-v6-38.json`). A 90-degree pushrod V6 with split pins for even firing: 96.5 x 86.4 mm (3791 cc), 9.4:1 (engines of the kind: 140 to 155 kW at 5200 rpm, 305 to 325 N m at 4000; makers' figures of the 1990s). A big front-drive sedan, four-speed automatic.

**Flat-plane 3.9 L V8, twin turbo** (`flat-plane-v8-39-twin-turbo.json`). A 3.9 L flat-plane V8 with a turbo a bank: 86.5 x 83 mm (3902 cc), 9.4:1, direct injection (engines of the kind: 450 to 530 kW at 7500 to 8000 rpm, 760 to 800 N m at 3000 to 5750; makers' figures). In a mid-engined coupe, seven-speed dual clutch.
